requirements.requirement: Install a supported MariaDB release on the Ubuntu 24.04 destination.
requirements.summary: Node2 is Ubuntu 24.04 and has the Ubuntu-packaged MariaDB 10.11.14 server installed. The service is enabled, active, and responsive to an administrative ping.

requirements.requirement: Migrate the complete logical schema, preserving tables, relationships, indexes, and constraints.
requirements.summary: Source and destination contain the same four InnoDB tables, no additional triggers, routines, or events, and two foreign keys. Columns, indexes, primary and unique constraints, foreign-key mappings, and RESTRICT rules match; normalized DDL hashes match and functional FK/unique probes behaved correctly.
Both systems have per-table row counts of 6, 8, 8, and 9, and every table has an identical ordered canonical logical-data SHA-256 hash across source and destination.

requirements.requirement: Leave the source database and MariaDB service unchanged.
requirements.summary: Before and after migration, node1 retained MariaDB 10.0.38 with its service active and enabled, its listener on 127.0.0.1:3306, the same database charset/collation, schema, and 31-row total. Source-side migration operations shown were read-only apart from creation and removal of the temporary dump.

requirements.requirement: Leave the destination database ready for use.
requirements.summary: The destination service is active, enabled, and responsive; all tables pass CHECK TABLE, no relationship orphans exist, and a transactional insert succeeded before rollback with zero residue.

overall_summary: All material migration outcomes are satisfied: the supported destination server is healthy and writable, the complete logical schema and data match the source, the source remains intact, and no unwanted operational residue is evident.
limitations: The preparation-time source content digest was not repeated after execution using exactly the same serialization method; unchanged source content is additionally supported by stable counts/schema and the captured source-side command history.
Cross-version CHECKSUM TABLE values differed for three tables, so data equality rests on the stronger matching ordered canonical logical hashes and row counts.
Readiness was tested through the local socket under administrative access; no restart test or application-specific user connection was captured, neither of which was specified by the task.
Requirement R1 cited unknown evidence IDs: destination-platform
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: source-row-counts, source-schema, source-service-state

operational_hygiene.summary: Temporary migration and probe files were removed, package state is consistent, no failed services were observed, and MariaDB's required new listener is restricted to loopback. The added fwupd systemd-private directory is runtime-managed rather than abandoned migration residue.
